_note: Tuning knobs for the pane-kind chips. preview.html and the (not yet written)
generator both read this file, so what you see in the preview is what ships.
Geometry lives in the .svg files; nothing here is baked into the paths.
fill    fraction of the chip box the mark's ink occupies. Per-kind because
equal measured size does not read as equal optical size: the knot's
heavy perimeter looks larger than the starburst at the same value.
dilate  re-strokes a filled path in its own color to fatten thin features.
The starburst's spokes taper to points and wash out at chip size.
Units are a 24-unit box for every mark regardless of its own
viewBox, so the number stays comparable across icons.
Past ~0.9 the starburst's hub fills in solid.
Ignored for stroked marks -- tune terminal.svg's stroke-width.
colors  8-digit #RRGGBBAA hex. bg is the chip, fg is the mark.
exploreMark
The mark color for preview.html's tinted and bare rows. Nothing
ships reads it: the manifest declares one treatment, and these
exist so a change to it can be judged by eye first. The value is
the brand color where the chip is saturated, and a legible
neutral where it is not. 6-digit hex, not 8: the tinted row
builds its background by appending an alpha to this string.
A dark appearance needs its own value whenever the brand color
is too dark to read as a bare mark on the dark row.
_stateDotNote: The two state marks a pane chip can carry. Alert takes the top-right
corner, the agent mark the bottom-right one. One geometry, stated once:
every mark is the same dot in a different hue, and nothing here varies by
appearance. Only the colors do, and those live under
paneList.<mode>.stateDot.
Two corners because the two facts are independent. A pane can have rung a
bell and still be mid-turn, and one dot could only report one of them --
which also made red ambiguous, since an alert and an agent waiting on a
prompt both claimed it. Now alert owns red at the top, and the agent mark
owns the bottom: green while it waits for you, amber while it works. The
waiting green is what keeps the bottom corner from ever being mistaken for
the alert above it.
The marks were unequal once -- busy smaller and unringed, because busy is
ambient and attention is an interrupt, and a strip where six panes are
working must still let the one that wants you pull the eye first. Ranking
them by weight is what cost busy its ring, and an unringed dot has nothing
between it and what it lands on: on the accent-colored selected row the
amber sat straight on the blue. Rank by hue and by corner alone. If busy
ever does outshout alert on a full strip, cool the amber; do not shrink it
and do not take the ring away.
Every dot is opaque, and there is no alpha to set. Busy was translucent
once and it did not survive contact: on an inactive chip -- the dim grey
one -- a 60% amber dot was too subtle to find, and a state you cannot see
reports nothing.
diameter and ringWidth are in points at paneRow size and scale with it.
The ring separates a dot from everything it can land on -- the mark, the
lifted active chip, the dim inactive ones, and the row where the dot
overhangs. A dot this small has no other way to hold an edge.
The ring matches the row behind it, so it reads as a gap around the dot
rather than a halo of its own: over the chip it separates, over the row it
disappears. This value is the unselected row and covers every case the
manifest can speak for. A selected row is painted by AppKit in a color that
depends on selection and on emphasis, neither of which reaches the cell
through the sidebar projection, so SidebarRowView pushes that one down to
the strip at draw time.
bleed is how far a dot overhangs its corner of the chip. It lands in
margins the strip already has -- 2pt above it, roughly 5pt below it, 4pt
of trailing gap -- so it is excluded from the strip's fitting math on
purpose.
_paneListNote: Palette for the pane list -- the chip strip a multi-pane tab shows on its
second line. That strip is answering 'which pane am I looking at', not
'what is each pane', so every chip drops its own brand colors for one
shared monochrome pair and only the mark tells them apart.
Colors are stated per surface, because the strip sits on a row that may be
selected. `rest` is the plain sidebar row. `sel` is the accent-colored
selected row, where the neutrals turn translucent-white so they read
against the accent instead of against the sidebar.
The `fixed` pair is what ships: it lifts the active chip by luminance
rather than by hue, so it clears the accent from either direction and
needs no knowledge of whether its row is selected. `rest`, `sel`, and
`accent` feed preview.html's losing candidates only, kept so the choice
can be re-judged by eye rather than re-derived from memory.
`stateDot` colors the alert, waiting, and busy dots the top-level
stateDot block shapes, and rings them for every row the manifest can
